<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><A name=item1a /><B>ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS.</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><I>An investment in our securities involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks described below, together with the other information contained in this Registration Statement, before making an investment decision. If any of the following risks actually occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations, and prospects could be materially and adversely affected. In such event, the trading price of our securities could decline, and investors could lose all or part of their investment.</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>&#160;</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><I>The risks described below are not the only risks facing the Company. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently consider immaterial may also impair our business operations.</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>RISKS RELATED TO OUR BUSINESS AND OPERATIONS</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We have had a history of operating losses and we may not sustain profitability.</I></B><I>&#160;</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:7.2pt'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The Company achieved net income of $70,000 for the year ended December 31, 2025, following a net loss of $471,000 for the year ended December 31, 2024. For the six months ended June 30, 2026, the Company recorded a net loss of $1,164,000, attributable in part to an approximately $970,000 net realizable value charge on slow-moving power supplies inventory. The Company has a history of fluctuating operating results and there is no assurance that management can sustain profitability. Continuing losses could materially adversely affect our financial stability and result in a decline in our stock price.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We face intense industry competition, price erosion and product obsolescence, which, in turn, could reduce our operating results.</I></B><I>&#160;</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We operate in an industry that is generally characterized by intense competition and rapid technological change. We believe that the principal bases of competition in our markets are breadth of product line, quality of products, stability, reliability and reputation of the provider, along with cost. Quantity discounts, price erosion, and rapid product obsolescence due to technological improvements are therefore common as competitors strive to retain or expand market share. Product obsolescence can lead to increases in unsellable inventory that may need to be written off and therefore could adversely affect our operating results. Similarly, price erosion can reduce our operating results by decreasing our revenues and our gross margins.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our long-term operating results depend substantially upon our ability to continually develop, introduce, and market new and innovative products, to modify existing products, to respond to technological change, and to customize certain products to meet customer requirements. There are numerous risks inherent in this process, including the risks that we will be unable to anticipate the direction of technological change or that we will be unable to develop and market new products and applications in a timely fashion to satisfy customer demands, which could result in a decrease in our net sales and a loss of market share to our competitors. Historically, we have had write-offs of excess and obsolete inventory that negatively impacted our results of operations. In the future, excess or obsolete inventory may need to be written off, and this in turn could reduce our operating results.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Changes in demand or downturns in the markets we serve could affect our business and operating results.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The markets for our products are cyclical and may experience downturns. Our target industries also experience volatility, and future volatility as well as downturns, and any failure of these industries to recover from downturns could materially harm our business and operating results. Likewise, if we have difficulty managing growth in our businesses, it could materially and adversely affect us. In addition, our business and financial position may be adversely affected by current and future economic conditions that cause a decline in business and consumer spending in the markets served by our or our customers&#8217; products.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>13</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Our operating results may be impaired if demand for our technology declines or fails to develop as we expect.</I></B><I>&#160;</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our revenues will decrease if demand for our products declines or if rising prices make it more difficult to sell them. If products incorporating other technologies gain comparable or superior market acceptance and competitive price advantage, our business, financial condition and operating results could be adversely and materially affected unless we successfully develop and market products incorporating the new technology. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Our principal competitors have substantially greater financial resources to devote to developing, marketing and selling their products. Consequently, we may be unable to maintain or increase our market share.</I></B><I>&#160;</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We face significant competition in developing and selling our products. Rapid and ongoing changes in technology and product standards could quickly render our products less competitive or even obsolete. We have significantly smaller financial, technical, manufacturing, marketing and other resources than many of our competitors and these limited resources may impair the operating results of our business in many ways. For example, in the past our competitors have offered wider ranges of products, expanded the geographic scope of their markets, acquired other companies, and developed or acquired proprietary technologies that operate in conjunction with their products. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>In the future, our competitors may leverage their greater resources to: </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:43.2pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>develop, manufacture and market products that are less expensive than or technologically superior to ours;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:43.2pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>reach a wider array of potential customers through a broader range of marketing and distribution channels;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:43.2pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>respond more quickly to new or changing technologies, customer requirements and standards; or&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:43.2pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>reduce prices in order to preserve or gain market share.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:7.2pt'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We believe competitive pressures are likely to continue. We cannot guarantee that our resources will be sufficient to address this competition or that we will manage costs and adopt strategies capable of effectively utilizing our resources. If we are unable to respond to competitive pressures successfully, our prices and profit margins may fall and our market share may decrease.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We rely on indirect sales channels to market and sell our branded storage products and both direct and indirect sales channels to market and sell our branded power solutions products. A loss of or deterioration in our relationship with one or more of our resellers or distributors, or our inability to establish new indirect sales channels to drive growth of our products, could negatively affect our operating results.</I></B><I>&#160;</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We sell the majority of our branded storage products to value-added resellers, who in turn sell our products to end users. In some cases, resellers integrate our tape libraries with products of other manufacturers and sell the combined products to their own customers. We sell our branded power solution products both direct to OEM customers (or their contract manufacturers) and to our distribution channel who in turn sell our products to OEM customers. The success of these sales channels is hard to predict and we have no purchase commitments or long-term orders from them that assure us of any baseline sales through these channels. Several of our resellers and distributors carry competing product lines that they may promote over our products, which may negatively impact our sales. A reseller or distributor might not continue to purchase our products or market them effectively, and each reseller or distributor determines the type and amount of our products that it will purchase from us and the pricing of the products that it sells to their customers. Establishing new indirect sales channels globally is an important part of our strategy to drive growth of our revenue.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Our operating results could be adversely affected by any number of factors, including: </I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>A change in competitive strategy that adversely affects a reseller&#8217;s or distributor&#8217;s willingness or ability to distribute our products;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Reaching fewer customers or losing sales due to ineffective efforts of resellers and distributors;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Reduced margins and increased costs associated with channel sales;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>An inability to gain traction in developing new indirect sales channels for our branded products;&nbsp;</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>14</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Any financial difficulties of our resellers, authorized distributors or direct OEM customers that result in their inability to pay amounts owed to us or effectively market our products;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Changes in requirements or programs that allow our products to be sold by third parties to government customers; or&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Changes in product requirements or certification programs that limit our ability for our products to be sold in our established current markets.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We do not have any exclusive agreements with our VARs or distributors, who purchase our products on an individual purchase order basis. If we lose important VARs or distributors, or if they reduce their focus on our products or if we are unable to obtain additional VARs, our business could be negatively affected.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:7.2pt'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>If our suppliers fail to meet our component and manufacturing needs, it could delay our production and our product shipments to customers and negatively affect our operations.</I></B><I>&#160;</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our products comprise many components and subassemblies produced by outside suppliers. We depend greatly on these suppliers for items that are essential to the manufacture of our products, including tape drives, printed circuit boards and integrated circuits. For certain items, we qualify only a single source, which magnifies the risk of shortages and decreases our ability to negotiate with that supplier on the basis of price. From time to time, we have been unable to obtain sufficient components due to shortages or quality issues from some of our suppliers. If our suppliers fail to meet our manufacturing needs, it would delay our production and our product shipments to customers and negatively affect our operations. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We also rely on software vendors to develop and support software needed for operation of our automated tape library products and their integration into the end-user&#8217;s computing environment. Accordingly, the continued development and future growth of the market for our tape library products will depend partly upon the ability of these vendors to meet the overall data storage and management needs of tape library purchasers and our ability to maintain relationships with these firms.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The primary suppliers of our N2Power power supplies are located in China. If a manufacturer should be unable to deliver products to us on a timely basis or at all, our power supply business could be adversely affected. Although we have had many years of favorable experience with these suppliers, there can be no assurance that circumstances might not change and compel one or more of these suppliers to curtail or terminate deliveries to us. Moreover, the use of contract manufacturers to provide our power supplies typically requires that we place production orders several months in advance of our expected need for the products. This in turn leads to risks that we may lack sufficient inventory to sell to our customers where our expectations were conservative, or that we may order excess product inventory where our expectations were optimistic. We have in the past, experienced shortages of some parts needed to manufacture our power supplies.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Issues such as natural disasters, pandemics, government-directed closures, geopolitical disruptions, or other unforeseen events may adversely affect our ability to deliver product in a timely manner to our customers.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We face potential product liability claims that could result in significant costs.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We face an inherent risk of exposure to product liability claims in the event that our products malfunction, fail, or cause personal injury or property damage. Our power supply products are integrated into a wide variety of customer applications, including medical devices, telecommunications infrastructure, and industrial equipment, where product failures could have serious consequences. We maintain limited product liability insurance, and there can be no assurance that such insurance will be sufficient to cover potential claims. Any product liability claim, with or without merit, could result in costly litigation, divert management attention, damage our reputation, and adversely affect our business and financial condition.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>15</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We may experience excess or obsolete inventory, which could adversely affect our financial results.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our products are subject to technological change and evolving industry standards, which may render existing inventory obsolete. In addition, we are required to purchase certain components and finished goods from our contract manufacturers with significant lead times, which requires us to forecast demand in advance. If actual demand is lower than forecasted, we may be left with excess inventory that we are unable to sell or that we must sell at reduced prices. In June 2026, we recorded a net realizable value charge of approximately $970,000 on slow-moving power supplies inventory due to decreased demand from our customers. We have experienced similar inventory challenges in the past and may experience them again in the future. Excess or obsolete inventory charges could reduce our gross profit and adversely affect our results of operations.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We are dependent on a limited number of customers for a significant portion of our revenue.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>A significant portion of our revenue has historically been derived from a relatively small number of customers. The loss of any one or more of our significant customers, or a significant reduction in orders from such customers, could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition, and results of operations. We do not have long-term purchase commitments from most of our customers, and they may reduce, delay, or cancel orders at any time. Our ability to maintain and grow our revenue depends on our success in retaining existing customers and attracting new customers.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>If we fail to develop and introduce new products on a timely and cost-effective basis, or if our products do not contain the features required by the marketplace, we may eventually lose market share and sales to competitors.</I></B><I>&#160;</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The market for our products is characterized by changing technology and evolving industry standards. Our future results will depend on our ability to anticipate changes in technology, to develop new and enhanced products on a timely and cost-effective basis, and to introduce, manufacture and achieve market acceptance of these new and enhanced products. With respect to our tape library products in particular, the introduction of new storage technologies or the adoption of an industry standard different from our current product standards could render our existing products obsolete.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:7.2pt'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Development schedules for high technology products are inherently subject to uncertainty and there can be no assurance that we will be able to meet our product development schedules or that our development costs will be within budgeted amounts. If the products or product enhancements developed are not deliverable due to technical problems, quality issues or component shortages, or if such products or product enhancements are not accepted by the marketplace or are unreliable, then our business, financial condition and results of operations may be adversely affected. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>If we fail to protect our intellectual property or if others use our proprietary technology without authorization, our competitive position may suffer.</I></B><I>&#160;</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We rely on a combination of trademark, trade secret, and other intellectual property laws and various contract rights to protect our proprietary rights. Despite our efforts to protect our proprietary rights, however, unauthorized parties may attempt to copy or otherwise obtain or use our products or technology. As a consequence, these rights may not preclude competitors from developing products that are substantially equivalent or superior to our products. In addition, many aspects of our products are not subject to intellectual property protection and therefore can be reproduced by others. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Intellectual property infringement claims brought against us could result&#160;in a substantial liability and significant costs, and as a result, our business, financial condition and operating results may be materially and adversely affected. </I></B></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>16</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>From time to time, we may become subject to claims or inquiries regarding an alleged unauthorized use by us of another party&#8217;s intellectual property. While we currently believe the amount of ultimate liability, if any, with respect to any such actions will not materially affect our financial position, results of operations or liquidity, the outcome of any license discussion or litigation is uncertain. Adverse resolution of any infringement claim could subject us to substantial liabilities and require us to refrain from manufacturing and selling certain products. In addition, the costs incurred in intellectual property litigation can be substantial, regardless of the outcome. As a result, our business, financial condition and operating results could be materially and adversely affected.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Undetected manufacturing flaws could increase our costs, reduce our revenues and divert resources from our core business needs.</I></B><I>&#160;</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Despite our efforts to revise and update our manufacturing and test processes to address engineering and component changes, we may not be able to control and eliminate manufacturing flaws adequately. These flaws may include undetected software or hardware defects associated with a newly introduced product, a new version of an existing product, or a product that has been integrated into a system or apparatus with the products of other vendors. If we fail to adequately monitor, develop and implement appropriate test and manufacturing processes we could experience a rate of product failure that results in substantial shipment delays, warranty costs or damage to our reputation. Product flaws may also consume our limited engineering resources and interrupt our development efforts. Significant product failures would increase our costs, result in the loss of future sales and be harmful to our business.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:7.2pt'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Much of our business is subject to risks associated with operations in foreign countries.</I></B><I>&#160;</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We generate a significant percentage of our revenue internationally, and we believe that international sales will continue to represent a substantial portion of our revenues. In addition, our manufacturing of power supply products is performed by contract manufacturers in Asia. We face risks that the countries in which we conduct business, or in which we have customers, suppliers, or contract manufacturers could:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Experience financial, economic or political instability;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Adopt laws that make the enforcement of our contractual or other legal rights and remedies difficult or uncertain;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Provide inadequate intellectual property protection for our technology;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Impose restrictions on the export or import of technology that would affect our ability to obtain supplies from, or sell products into, such countries;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Impose tariffs, quotas, taxes, other market barriers;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Impose other laws, regulations or policies adversely affecting trade, investment or taxes, including those relating to the repatriation of funds and to withholding taxes; or&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Experience business closures due to health threats or natural disasters.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Other risks and costs associated with international operations include:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Currency exchange risk, to the extent that exchange rate fluctuations could make our products unaffordable to foreign purchasers or more expensive compared to those of foreign manufacturers;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Compliance with laws and regulations in various regions in which we operate;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Greater difficulty and longer delays in collecting accounts receivable from international customers; or&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Increased risk of shipping disruptions particularly in foreign countries experiencing political instability.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We are subject to cybersecurity risks that could adversely affect our business.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We rely on information technology systems and networks to conduct our business, process transactions, and maintain records. These systems are subject to cybersecurity threats, including unauthorized access, ransomware attacks, phishing, and other forms of cyberattack. A significant cybersecurity incident could result in the loss of proprietary information, disruption to our operations, damage to our reputation, regulatory penalties, or financial losses. While we have implemented measures to protect our information technology infrastructure, there can be no assurance that these measures will be sufficient to prevent all cybersecurity breaches. The costs of preventing, mitigating, and recovering from cybersecurity incidents could be material.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>17</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:7.2pt'>&#160;&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Change of board and senior management, and retention of key personnel. </I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Turnover in key management positions could temporarily harm our financial performance and results of operations. Loss of certain members of our senior management may disrupt operations and relations with key customers and distributors and our operating results could be adversely affected. Our capacity to develop and implement new technologies depends on our ability to employ personnel with highly technical skills. If we cannot attract and retain key technical personnel, our technical expertise may suffer, and our operating results could be adversely affected. In addition, it could be difficult, time-consuming and expensive to replace any key management member or other critical personnel and no guarantee exists that we will be able to recruit suitable replacements or assimilate new key management personnel into our organization to achieve our operating objectives. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Our success depends in large part on our CEO, who simultaneously leads other public corporations.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Steven N. Bronson, our Chief Executive Officer and President, simultaneously serves as the President and Chief Executive Officer of Interlink Electronics, Inc. (NASDAQ: LINK) (&#8220;<B><I>Interlink</I></B>&#8221;), and Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of BKF Capital Group, Inc. (OTCMKTS: BKFG) (&#8220;<B><I>BKF Capital</I></B>&#8221;). As a result, he divides his time among these companies and does not devote his full business time and attention to Qualstar&#8217;s business. Mr. Bronson currently works on average approximately 20 to 30 hours per week for Qualstar. There can be no assurance, however, that the amount of time Mr. Bronson devotes to our Company will not diminish from time to time for limited or extended periods as his other business obligations require a greater portion of his attention. Mr. Bronson is not required to spend a minimum amount of time on Qualstar business. Our continued success depends in part upon the availability and performance of Mr. Bronson, who possesses unique and extensive industry knowledge and experience as well as a deep understanding of our business and strategy. A reduction in Mr. Bronson&#8217;s services to Qualstar from their current levels due to his obligations to Interlink, BKF Capital or other organizations with which he is affiliated could have a disruptive effect, adversely impacting our ability to manage our business effectively and execute our business strategy.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Our revenues and operating results may fluctuate materially from quarter to quarter, which may in turn affect our stock price. </I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our quarterly revenues and operating results have fluctuated in the past and are likely to vary in the future due to the various factors discussed above and others, including: </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:43.2pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>General economic conditions affecting spending and the rates of growth or decline in the markets we serve;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:43.2pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Variations in product order backlogs, and reductions in the size, delays in the timing, or cancellation of significant customer orders;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:43.2pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>The timing of introductions and marketplace acceptance of new or enhanced products by us or our competitors;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:43.2pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Expansions or reductions in our relationships with distributors, VARs or OEM customers;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:43.2pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Unprofitable investments in engineering activities, or sales evaluation, testing, and acceptance processes;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:43.2pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Unforeseen warranty costs that exceed established reserves;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:43.2pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Timing and levels of our operating expenses; or&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:43.2pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Emerging new technologies that change the nature of or need for our products.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:14.7pt'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We believe that period-to-period comparisons of our operating results may not necessarily be reliable indicators of our future performance. It is likely that in some future period our operating results will not meet your expectations or those of public market analysts. Any unanticipated change in revenues or operating results is likely to cause our stock price to fluctuate since such changes reflect new information not previously available to investors and analysts. New information may cause investors and analysts to revalue our stock and this, in the aggregate, may cause fluctuations in our stock price.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>18</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Changes in trade policy in the United States and other countries, including changes in trade agreements and the imposition of tariffs and the resulting consequences, may have adverse impacts on our business, results of operations and financial condition.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The United States government has imposed, and may continue to impose, tariffs on a wide range of products imported from China and other countries. Given that our primary contract manufacturer for N2Power power supplies and a significant product supplier are located in China, these tariffs have had, and may continue to have, a direct and material impact on the cost of our products and components. We may not be able to fully pass on increased costs to our customers, which could reduce our gross margins and adversely affect our competitive position. In addition, retaliatory tariffs imposed by other countries on U.S. goods could adversely affect our ability to sell our products in international markets. We cannot predict future trade policy, the terms of any renegotiated trade agreements, or additional tariffs and their impact on our business. To the extent that trade tariffs and other restrictions increase the price of, or limit the amount of, our products or components imported into the United States or other countries, or create adverse tax consequences, the cost or gross margin of our products may be adversely affected and demand from our customers may diminish. If we deem it necessary to alter all or a portion of our supply chain or operations in response to such policies, our capital and operating costs may increase, and such efforts may take time to implement and may result in adverse or fluctuating financial results. As a result, changes in international trade policy and tariffs could adversely affect our business, results of operations and financial condition.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>19</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>RISKS RELATED TO OUR SECURITIES</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;<I>Trading in our stock has historically been limited and our stock price has been volatile, which may affect your ability to sell your shares.</I></B><I>&#160;</I></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The average trading volume in our stock has been historically low, with little or no trading at all on some days. &nbsp;Combined with the factors listed below, this has caused the price of our stock to be volatile. Consequently, it may be difficult to sell your shares of our stock at the price you paid for them or at a price equal to that quoted on the OTC Markets. Factors that may cause our stock price to fluctuate in the future include:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Quarterly variations in operating results, especially if they differ from our previously announced forecasts or forecasts made by analysts;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Announcements by us of anticipated future revenues or operating results, or by others concerning us, our competitors, our customers, or our industry;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>The introduction of new technology or products by us or our competitors;&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Comments about us and the data storage or power supply markets made by industry analysts or on Internet comment sites; or&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Changes in earnings estimates by analysts or changes in accounting policies; in product pricing policies by us or our competitors; or in general economic conditions.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:7.2pt'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>In addition, stock markets experience periods of extreme price and volume volatility. This volatility has a substantial effect on the market prices of securities of many smaller public companies for reasons frequently unrelated or disproportionate to the operating performance of the specific companies. These market fluctuations may adversely affect the market price of our common stock.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Our common stock is quoted on the OTC Markets and may be subject to limited liquidity and substantial volatility.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our common stock is quoted on the OTC Markets. Securities quoted on the OTC Markets frequently experience limited liquidity, reduced trading volume, substantial price volatility, limited analyst coverage, and reduced institutional investor participation compared to securities listed on national securities exchanges. As a result, stockholders may experience difficulty buying or selling shares at desired prices or at all. The market price of our common stock may fluctuate significantly and may not reflect the underlying value of our business or assets.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Our common stock may be deemed a &#8220;penny stock,&#8221; which may reduce liquidity and investor interest.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>If our common stock is deemed to constitute a &#8220;penny stock&#8221; under applicable securities laws, broker-dealers may become subject to additional regulatory requirements relating to transactions involving our securities. These requirements may discourage broker-dealers from recommending or executing transactions in our securities, which could adversely affect liquidity and investor interest. The penny stock rules require, among other things, that any broker-dealer who recommends our securities to persons other than established customers and accredited investors must, prior to the sale, deliver a standardized risk disclosure document that provides information about penny stocks and the risks in the penny stock market. The broker-dealer must also provide the customer with current bid and offer quotations for the penny stock, the compensation of the broker-dealer and its salesperson in the transaction, and monthly account statements showing the market value of each penny stock held in the customer&#8217;s account. These additional requirements may have the effect of reducing trading activity in the secondary market for our common stock.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>20</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Future sales or issuances of our common stock could depress the market price of our shares.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Sales of a substantial number of shares of our common stock in the public market, or the perception that such sales could occur, could adversely affect the market price of our common stock and could impair our future ability to raise capital through the sale of equity securities. In addition, we may issue additional shares of common stock or securities convertible into common stock in connection with future financings, acquisitions, employee benefit plans, or otherwise. Any such issuance could result in dilution to existing stockholders and could cause the market price of our common stock to decline.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We are a &#8220;smaller reporting company&#8221; and the reduced disclosure requirements applicable to smaller reporting companies may make our common stock less attractive to investors.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We qualify as a &#8220;smaller reporting company&#8221; as defined in the Exchange Act. As such, we are permitted to take advantage of certain reduced disclosure and reporting requirements, including providing only two years of audited financial statements, reduced executive compensation disclosure, and exemption from the auditor attestation requirement on internal controls over financial reporting under Section 404(b) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act. We cannot predict whether investors will find our common stock less attractive because of our reliance on these exemptions. If some investors find our common stock less attractive as a result, there may be a less active trading market for our common stock and our stock price may be more volatile.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We do not intend to pay cash dividends on our common stock for the foreseeable future.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We have never declared or paid cash dividends on our common stock and do not currently intend to pay such dividends in the foreseeable future. We presently intend to retain any future earnings to support operations, software development activities, commercialization initiatives, infrastructure expansion, and business growth. As a result, capital appreciation, if any, of our common stock will be the sole source of gain for the foreseeable future.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>RISKS RELATED TO OUR CORPORATE STRUCTURE AND GOVERNANCE</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We are controlled by our principal stockholder, which may limit your ability to influence corporate matters.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Steven N. Bronson, our Chief Executive Officer and President, together with BKF Capital and its subsidiary BKF Asset Holdings, Inc., which are controlled by Mr. Bronson, beneficially owns a majority of our outstanding common stock. As a result, Mr. Bronson has the ability to control all matters submitted to our stockholders for approval, including the election and removal of directors, amendments to our articles of incorporation and bylaws, and any merger, consolidation, sale of all or substantially all of our assets, or other major corporate transactions. This concentration of ownership may discourage, delay, or prevent a change of control of our Company, which could deprive our stockholders of an opportunity to receive a premium for their shares. In addition, the interests of Mr. Bronson may not always coincide with the interests of other stockholders.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Our Board of Directors has only two members and may lack sufficient independent oversight.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our Board of Directors (the &#8220;<B><I>Board</I></B>&#8221;) currently consists of only two members, one of whom is our Chief Executive Officer and is therefore not independent. As a result, we may lack the breadth of experience, diversity of perspectives, and level of independent oversight typically associated with larger boards. The limited size of our Board may also make it more difficult to establish and maintain fully independent audit, compensation, and nominating committees, which could affect the quality of our corporate governance and our ability to attract institutional investors.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We do not currently have a separately designated audit committee or a formally adopted code of ethics.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The Company does not currently maintain a separately designated audit committee. The functions typically performed by an audit committee are presently performed by the Board. In addition, the Company has not yet adopted a formal written code of ethics applicable to its principal executive officer, principal financial officer, or principal accounting officer. The absence of an audit committee and a formal code of ethics may increase the risk of financial misstatement, fraud, or inadequate oversight of related-party transactions, and may adversely affect investor confidence in the Company.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>21</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Conflicts of interest may arise from our management&#8217;s roles with affiliated companies.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our Chief Executive Officer, Steven N. Bronson, simultaneously serves as the Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of Interlink and as Chairman, President and Chief Executive Officer of BKF Capital. Our Acting Chief Financial Officer, Ryan J. Hoffman, simultaneously serves as the Chief Financial Officer of both Interlink and BKF Capital. We also engage in various related-party transactions with these affiliated companies, including mutual facilities sharing agreements and consulting arrangements. These overlapping management roles and related-party transactions create potential conflicts of interest. There can be no assurance that any conflicts of interest will be resolved in our favor, and decisions made by our management in the context of their multiple roles may not always reflect the best interests of Qualstar or its stockholders. Furthermore, the time and attention that Messrs. Bronson and Hoffman devote to their responsibilities at affiliated companies may limit their availability to manage our business.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Our Articles of Incorporation opt out of certain Nevada anti-takeover statutes, which may have differing effects on stockholders.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our Articles of Incorporation expressly elect not to be governed by the Nevada Revised Statutes, or NRS, Chapter 78.411-78.444, relating to combinations with interested stockholders, or NRS 78.378-78.3793, inclusive, relating to control share acquisitions. This opt-out may facilitate potential acquisitions and provide stockholders with opportunities to sell their shares at a premium, but it also removes protections that could otherwise deter coercive or unfair takeover attempts. In addition, our Articles require the affirmative vote of the holders of at least two-thirds (2/3) of the voting power of all outstanding shares entitled to vote to approve certain business combinations, including mergers, consolidations, share exchanges, sales or other dispositions of substantially all of our assets, or our dissolution, unless the transaction has been approved by a majority of the Board. This supermajority requirement could delay or prevent transactions that stockholders might otherwise view as favorable, especially given the concentrated ownership of Mr. Bronson and his affiliates.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Our Bylaws contain exclusive forum provisions that could limit stockholders&#8217; ability to obtain a favorable judicial forum for disputes.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our Bylaws provide that, unless we consent in writing to an alternative forum, the state courts located in Nevada (or, if those courts lack subject matter jurisdiction, the federal district courts located in Nevada) are the sole and exclusive forum for derivative actions, claims for breach of fiduciary duty, claims arising under the NRS, our Articles or our Bylaws, and claims governed by the internal affairs doctrine. The federal district courts of the United States are the exclusive forum for claims arising under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the &#8220;<B><I>Securities Act</I></B>&#8221;), or similar federal securities laws. These provisions could increase the costs for stockholders seeking to bring claims in other jurisdictions and may discourage stockholders from bringing lawsuits.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Our Board of Directors has broad authority to amend our Bylaws without stockholder approval, and certain Bylaw provisions require a supermajority stockholder vote to amend.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Pursuant to our Articles and Bylaws, the Board may adopt, amend, or repeal the Bylaws without stockholder approval. Certain provisions&#8212;including the indemnification provisions in our Articles, the exclusive forum provision our Bylaws, and Section 8.6 of our Bylaws itself &#8212;may not be amended or repealed, nor may any provision inconsistent with them be adopted, without the affirmative vote of both the Board and the holders of at least two-thirds (2/3) of the outstanding shares entitled to vote thereon. This concentration of authority in the Board, together with the supermajority requirements combined with the concentrated ownership of Mr. Bronson and his affiliates, could limit stockholders&#8217; ability to effect changes to the Company&#8217;s governance.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>22</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Our Bylaws establish a 25% ownership threshold for stockholders to call special meetings, which may limit minority stockholder rights.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our Bylaws require one or more stockholders holding, in the aggregate, at least 25% of the voting power of the outstanding shares entitled to vote on the proposed matter to request that the Board call a special meeting, subject to procedural and informational requirements. These requirements include identifying the specific business, signing and dating the request, providing evidence of ownership, undertaking to maintain the required ownership level through the meeting, and appearing in person or by proxy. This threshold, combined with the concentrated ownership of Mr. Bronson and his affiliates, may effectively prevent minority stockholders from calling special meetings.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Nevada law limits the personal liability of our directors and officers, and our governing documents provide broad indemnification, which may discourage stockholder lawsuits.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our Articles eliminate, to the fullest extent permitted by the NRS, the personal liability of our directors and officers for damages for breach of fiduciary duty, except for acts or omissions involving intentional misconduct, fraud, or a knowing violation of law. Our Articles and Bylaws provide mandatory indemnification and advancement of expenses for directors and officers, including a standard under which indemnification may be denied under the Bylaws only upon a specific finding, based on clear and convincing evidence, that the conduct involved intentional misconduct, fraud, or a knowing violation of law. These provisions may reduce the likelihood of stockholder derivative suits and limit stockholders&#8217; ability to obtain monetary damages from our directors and officers.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>RISKS RELATED TO BEING A REPORTING COMPANY</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We will incur substantial costs as a reporting company, which may strain our financial resources.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Upon effectiveness of this Registration Statement, the Company will become subject to the reporting requirements of the Exchange Act, including the obligation to file annual, quarterly, and current reports with the SEC. Compliance with these obligations will require substantial accounting, legal, compliance, auditing, administrative, and management resources. These costs may be significant relative to the Company&#8217;s current scale of operations and may divert resources from business development and commercialization activities.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>In particular, the Company expects to incur significant additional costs related to audit and accounting fees, legal fees, SEC filing fees, directors&#8217; and officers&#8217; liability insurance premiums, investor relations activities, and compliance with the Sarbanes-Oxley Act of 2002. These costs may be disproportionately burdensome relative to the Company&#8217;s current scale of operations, depending on the complexity of its operations and the level of professional services required. These increased costs may reduce the Company&#8217;s net income and available cash resources and could divert management&#8217;s time and attention from business operations.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>We may have difficulty maintaining effective internal controls over financial reporting.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>As a reporting company, we will be required to maintain effective disclosure controls and internal controls over financial reporting. Given our limited personnel, and reliance on third-party service providers, we may experience difficulty designing, implementing, and maintaining effective internal controls. If we fail to maintain effective internal controls, we may be unable to accurately report our financial results or comply with SEC reporting obligations, which could result in regulatory scrutiny, restatements, loss of investor confidence, or other adverse consequences.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Failure to comply with reporting obligations could adversely affect our business and securities.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Failure to timely file required reports or otherwise comply with applicable securities laws, SEC regulations, OTC Markets requirements, or other reporting obligations could result in enforcement actions, fines, trading suspensions, reduced market visibility, or removal from quotation on the OTC Markets. Any such actions could materially and adversely affect our business, reputation and operations and the liquidity and market price of our securities.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>23</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>Overview </B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Qualstar is a custom designer and one-stop provider of enterprise archival data storage hardware and software solutions. We also sell compact, high-efficiency power supply solutions through our N2Power subsidiary. Our data storage systems are marketed under the Qualstar brand and include highly scalable automated magnetic tape libraries and software used to store, retrieve and manage electronic data primarily in the network computing environment. Our data storage solutions include models ranging from entry-level to enterprise and are a cost-effective resource for organizations requiring backup, recovery and archival storage of critical electronic information. The distribution channels for our data storage devices include resellers, system integrators, and original equipment manufacturers (&#8220;OEMs&#8221;). In addition, the Company is a leading provider of standard, modified-standard and custom-designed power supply solutions marketed under the N2Power brand. Our power supply solutions give OEMs and product designers more functionality while reducing thermal loads, cooling requirements, and operating costs. We currently sell our power supply solutions to OEMs across a wide range of markets, including telecom/networking equipment, audio/visual, industrial, gaming and medical.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Qualstar Corporation was incorporated in California in 1984 and re-incorporated in Nevada in January 2026. It has three wholly owned subsidiaries: the N2Power, Inc. subsidiary (&#8220;N2Power&#8221;) operates the Company&#8217;s power supplies business; the Q-Smart Data Limited (China) subsidiary pursues new data storage business opportunities in Asia; and. the Qualstar Limited (U.K.) subsidiary supports expansion of the Company&#8217;s data storage business in the United Kingdom, Europe and Africa.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We sell our products globally through authorized resellers and distributors and directly to OEMs. Our data storage products are manufactured by our OEM suppliers in other parts of the world and configured to order by us at our facility in Camarillo, California, or at our facility in Shenzhen, China, or by our fulfillment and logistics partner in Warsaw, Poland. N2Power uses contract manufacturers in Asia to produce our power supply solutions.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>The fluctuations in revenues for the three and six months ended June&#160;30, 2026 compared to the prior year are attributable to the segment-specific factors described below.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Segment Revenue</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Data Storage</I></B> &#8211;&nbsp;For the three months ended June&#160;30, 2026, data storage revenues were up 58% compared to the same quarter in 2025, which was attributable to an 80% increase in product revenue from higher shipments of our tape-based data storage products and solutions, offset in part by a 19% decrease in revenues from technical service and support contracts. For the six months ended June&#160;30, 2026, data storage revenues were up 31% compared to the same period in 2025, which was attributable to a 46% increase in product revenue from higher shipments of our tape-based data storage products and solutions, offset in part by a 24% decrease in revenues from technical service and support contracts.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Power Supplies</I></B> &#8211;&nbsp;The 14% and 50% decreases in power supplies revenues in the three-month and six-month periods ended June&#160;30, 2026, respectively, compared to the prior-year periods were due to decreased customer demand and order fulfilment of our power supplies products.</P>

Excluding this charge, gross margin percentages were 36.4% and 32.2% for the three and six months ended June&#160;30, 2026, respectively.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Engineering</I></B>. Engineering expenses for the three- and six-month periods ended June 30, 2026 were generally consistent with the corresponding prior-year periods, except that the prior-year periods included $31,000 of Employee Retention Credits (&#8220;<B><I>ERCs</I></B>&#8221;), which reduced engineering expenses in those prior year periods.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Sales and Marketing</I></B>. Sales and marketing expenses increased for the three- and six-month periods ended June 30, 2026 compared with the corresponding prior-year periods due to higher marketing and promotional activities and trade show costs, as well as the absence of $63,000 and $119,000 of ERCs recorded in the prior-year three- and six-month periods, respectively, which reduced sales and marketing expenses in those prior year periods.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>General and Administrative</I></B>. General and administrative expenses for the three- and six-month periods ended June 30, 2026 were generally consistent with the corresponding prior-year periods, except that the six-month period ended June&#160;30, 2025 included ERCs of $39,000, which reduced general and administrative expenses in that prior year period.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>26</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Other Income (Expense), net</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Other income (expense), net for the three months ended June&#160;30, 2026 included $10,000 of interest income and $301,000 of losses on marketable securities. Other income (expense), net for the three months ended June&#160;30, 2025 included $35,000 of interest income, $8,000 of gains on foreign currency exchange, and $156,000 of gains on marketable securities. Other income (expense), net for the six months ended June&#160;30, 2026 included $23,000 of interest income, $1,000 of losses on foreign currency exchange, and $139,000 of losses on marketable securities. Other income (expense), net for the six months ended June&#160;30, 2025 included $76,000 of interest income, $27,000 of gains on foreign currency exchange, and $145,000 of gains on marketable securities.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Liquidity and Capital Resources </I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Cash and cash equivalents decreased $739,000 to $1,129,000 at June&#160;30, 2026, from $1,868,000 at December&#160;31, 2025.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Operating Activities</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Net cash used in operating activities was $675,000 for the six months ended June&#160;30, 2026, compared with cash provided by operating activities of $208,000 for the first half of 2025. Cash used in operating activities in 2026 was the result of net loss of $1,164,000, non-cash expenses of $18,000, non-cash losses on marketable securities of $139,000, and cash provided by changes in operating assets and liabilities of $332,000. Cash provided by operations in 2025 was the result of net income of $387,000, non-cash expenses of $100,000, gains on marketable securities of $204,000, and cash used in changes in operating assets and liabilities of $75,000.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Investing Activities</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Cash used in investing activities for the six months ended June&#160;30, 2026 and 2025 consisted of $64,000 and $202,000, respectively, of net purchases of marketable securities.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Financing Activities </I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:54pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:54pt;color:#000000'>No cash was provided by or used in financing activities for the six months ended June&#160;30, 2026. Cash used in financing activities for the six months ended June&#160;30, 2025 consisted of $218,000 used to repurchase shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock under the Company&#8217;s Stock Repurchase Program (the &#8220;<B><I>Stock Repurchase Program</I></B>&#8221;). The Stock Repurchase Program, which was extended in March 2025, permits the repurchase of up to 100,000 shares of common stock through December 31, 2026. Share repurchases under the program are discretionary and may be suspended or discontinued at any time.</P>
