<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>The fluctuations in revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to the prior year are attributable to the segment-specific factors described below.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Segment Revenue</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Data Storage </I></B>&#8211; For the year ended December 31, 2025, data storage revenues increased 9% compared to 2024, attributable to a 14% increase in product revenues, offset in part by a 9% decrease in revenues from technical service and support contracts.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Power Supplies </I></B>&#8211; The 64% decrease in power supplies revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to 2024 was due to decreased customer demand and order fulfillment of our power supplies products, caused primarily by the loss of a large customer.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Engineering</I></B>. Engineering expenses decreased 56% for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to 2024, due to a decrease in power supplies engineering employees and consultants engaged.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Sales and Marketing</I></B>. Sales and marketing expenses decreased 29% for the year ended December 31, 2025 compared to 2024 due to lower compensation costs on lower headcount of sales employees and consultants.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>General and Administrative</I></B>. General and administrative costs for the year ended December 31, 2025 were flat with 2024.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Other Income (Expense), net</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Other income (expense), net for the year ended December 31, 2025 included $115,000 of interest income, $31,000 of gains on foreign currency exchange, and $268,000 of net gains on marketable securities. Other income (expense) for the year ended December 31, 2024 included $80,000 of interest income, $28,000 of losses on foreign currency exchange, and $49,000 of net losses on marketable securities.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Liquidity and Capital Resources</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Cash and cash equivalents decreased $535,000 to $1,868,000 at December 31, 2025, from $2,403,000 at December 31, 2024.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Operating Activities</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Net cash provided by operating activities was $316,000 for the year ended December 31, 2025, compared with $222,000 for 2024. Cash provided by operating activities in 2025 was the result of net income of $70,000, non-cash expenses of $200,000 (consisting primarily of $191,000 of stock-based compensation expense and $7,000 of depreciation and amortization), non-cash gains on marketable securities of $268,000, and cash provided by changes in operating assets and liabilities of $314,000, including a $596,000 decrease in inventories and a $6,000 decrease in accounts receivable, partially offset by a $153,000 decrease in accounts payable and a $75,000 decrease in deferred service revenue. Cash provided by operating activities in 2024 was the result of net loss of $471,000, non-cash expenses of $196,000, non-cash losses on marketable securities of $49,000, and cash provided by changes in operating assets and liabilities of $448,000, including a $1,493,000 decrease in accounts receivable and a $75,000 decrease in inventories, partially offset by a $976,000 decrease in accounts payable.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Investing</I> <I>Activities</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Cash used in investing activities for the year ended December 31, 2025 consisted of $633,000 of net purchases of marketable securities. Cash provided by investing activities for the year ended December 31, 2024 consisted of $49,000 of proceeds from net sales of marketable securities. For the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, cash used in investing activities consisted of $64,000 and $202,000, respectively, of net purchases of marketable securities.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Financing</I> Activities</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Cash used in financing activities for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024 consisted of $218,000 and $143,000, respectively, used to repurchase shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock under the Stock Repurchase Program. No cash was provided by or used in financing activities for the six months ended June 30, 2026. Cash used in financing activities for the six months ended June 30, 2025 consisted of $218,000 used to repurchase shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock under the Stock Repurchase Program.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Sources of Liquidity and Capital</I></B>.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>The Company&#8217;s primary sources of liquidity are its existing cash and cash equivalents, marketable securities, and cash generated from operations. The Company does not currently have any bank credit facilities, revolving lines of credit, or other external debt financing arrangements. The Company has no outstanding indebtedness as of the date of this Registration Statement.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>The Company&#8217;s marketable securities consist of equity securities classified as available-for-sale and recorded at fair value. As of June 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025, the Company held $868,000 and $943,000, respectively, in marketable securities, which are subject to market risk and may fluctuate in value. These securities provide an additional source of liquidity that could be accessed through market sales, subject to market conditions.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Material Cash Requirements and Contractual Obligations</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>The Company&#8217;s material cash requirements include the following:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Lease Obligations</I></B>. The Company leases its headquarters and main facility, a 9,910 square-foot office and warehouse in Camarillo, California, under a lease extended through July 31, 2027 at $13,296 per month with a 3% annual step-up. The Company also leases a 560 square-foot office in Singapore on a month-to-month basis for approximately $1,600 per month. Total future minimum lease payments under these leases are approximately $259,000 as of December 31, 2025.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Operating Expenses</I></B>. The Company requires cash to fund its ongoing operations, including employee compensation, marketing and sales activities, engineering, and general and administrative costs. The Company&#8217;s total operating expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025 were $2,425,000.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Capital Expenditures</I></B>. The Company&#8217;s capital expenditure requirements are minimal. The Company did not make any material capital expenditures during the year ended December 31, 2025, and does not expect material capital expenditure requirements in the near term.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Public Company Costs</I></B>. Upon effectiveness of this Registration Statement, the Company expects to incur significant incremental costs associated with being a reporting company under the Exchange Act, including audit and accounting fees, legal fees, SEC filing fees, directors&#8217; and officers&#8217; liability insurance premiums, investor relations activities, and compliance costs. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Capital Sufficiency</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>We believe that our existing cash and cash equivalents, marketable securities, and cash flows from our operating activities will be sufficient to fund our working capital, capital expenditure needs, lease obligations, and anticipated incremental public company costs for at least twelve months from the date of this Registration Statement. This belief is based on our current operating plan, which assumes continuation of current revenue trends in our data storage segment, management of operating expenses at or below current levels, and no significant unanticipated expenditures.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>30</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>However, if we experience a sustained decline in revenues, a significant increase in operating expenses, or if we pursue acquisitions or strategic investments, we may require additional capital. The Company does not currently have any committed external sources of financing, and there can be no assurance that additional funding will be available to us when needed or, if available, that it can be obtained on commercially reasonable terms. If we are unable to generate sufficient cash from operations or obtain additional financing, we may be required to reduce or delay planned expenditures, curtail our growth strategy, or take other actions that could adversely affect our business.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>We may utilize cash to invest in or acquire businesses, products or technologies that we believe are additive to the strategic expansion of the Company. We periodically evaluate other companies and technologies for possible investment or acquisition. In addition, we have made, and may in the future make, investments in companies with whom we have identified potential synergies. However, we have no present commitments or agreements with respect to any material investment in or acquisition of other businesses or technologies.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Off-Balance Sheet Arrangements</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>As of December 31, 2025 and June 30, 2026, the Company did not have any off-balance sheet arrangements, as defined in Item 303(a)(4)(ii) of Regulation S-K.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The Company&#8217;s financial statements are prepared in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The preparation of financial statements requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenue, expenses, and related disclosures. Actual results could differ from those estimates.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Management believes the Company&#8217;s significant accounting policies include revenue recognition, related-party transaction accounting, fair value of financial instruments, stock-based compensation, debt and conversion feature evaluation, income taxes, and going concern assessment. These accounting policies are described in the notes to the Company&#8217;s financial statements included elsewhere in this Registration Statement.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><A name=item3 /><B>ITEM 3.</B> <B>PROPERTIES.</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Qualstar&#8217;s headquarters and main facility is located in Camarillo, California. The facility is 9,910 square feet, and the lease has been extended through July 31, 2027. Rent on this facility is approximately $13,000 per month. Qualstar permits Interlink to use a portion of the facility and is reimbursed for the space and related expenses on a monthly basis.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Through July 31, 2026, the Company leased a 1,400 square-foot office facility in Camarillo, California on a month-to-month basis. The rent on this facility was $1,900 per month.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Qualstar leases a 560 square-foot office in Singapore on a month-to-month basis for approximately $1,600 per month. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Qualstar previously leased a 7,287 square-foot facility in Shenzhen, China for approximately $3,500 per month under a lease that expired in May 2024.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Under a mutual facilities sharing agreement, Qualstar previously used portions of Interlink&#8217;s offices in Irvine, California and Bellevue, Washington. Through December 31, 2025, Qualstar used a portion of Interlink&#8217;s Irvine office and paid a facility usage fee of approximately $1,600 per month; from July 2024 to March 2025, it used a portion of Interlink&#8217;s Bellevue office and paid approximately $4,300 per month.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Biographies: </I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt'><B><I>Steven N. Bronson</I></B>. Mr. Bronson has served as our Chief Executive Officer and a member of our board since July 3, 2013. Mr. Bronson has over 40 years of business and entrepreneurial experience with a strong background in investment banking, operations and management. Mr. Bronson has been Chairman and President and Chief Executive Officer of BKF Capital (OTCMKTS: BKFG), a publicly traded company operating through its wholly owned subsidiary, BKF Asset Holdings, Inc., which invests in publicly and privately owned businesses, since September 2008. In addition, he has served as Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Interlink Electronics, Inc. (Nasdaq: LINK) (&#8220;<B><I>Interlink</I></B>&#8221;), a leading global provider of advanced sensing technologies and printed electronics solutions that enable Human-Machine Interface devices and Internet-of-Things applications. Mr. Bronson also serves as Chairman and President and Chief Executive Officer of Ridgefield Acquisition Corp. a public shell that is seeking a merger, acquisition, or business combination with a viable operating entity. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt'><B><I>David J. Wolenski</I></B>. Mr. Wolenski currently serves as President of Electro-Mechanical Products, Inc. (&#8220;EMP&#8221;), a privately held company engaged in the manufacture of precision-machined components and thermal management systems for the semiconductor, laser, and medical device industries. He has been a director on EMP&#8217;s board since August 2000. &nbsp;From 1996 to 2000, Mr. Wolenski was Chief Executive Officer of OZO Automation, Inc. (OTCBB:OZOA), a publicly traded company that produced robotic workstations for the electronics industry. In addition, he has also served as a member of the board of directors of Interlink since 2020. His past board affiliations have included OZO Automation, Inc. where he was a director from 1996-1999, and Bio-Medical Automation, Inc., where he was a director from 1999-2000. Mr. Wolenski holds a BS degree in Mechanical Engineering from the University of Colorado at Boulder (1983), and an MBA from the University of Colorado at Denver (1990). </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt'><B><I>Ryan Hoffman</I></B>. Mr. Hoffman has served as our Acting Chief Financial Officer since March 2024. &nbsp;Since 2020, Mr. Hoffman has also served as Chief Financial Officer of Interlink following 20&#160;years of public accounting and professional services experience at global public accounting firms, including 16&#160;years at RSM (having served as an audit partner) and four&#160;years at Ernst&#160;&amp; Young. Ryan graduated from Chapman University with a degree in accounting and is a licensed CPA (inactive). He is also the Chief Financial Officer of BKF Capital.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><A name=item6 /><B>ITEM 6. EXECUTIVE COMPENSATION</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>Overview </B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>Qualstar&#8217;s executive compensation program is based on the following principles:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Compensation fosters the long-term focus required for Qualstar&#8217;s success. In general, the compensation of Company executives includes longer-term incentives because they are in a greater position to influence longer-term results.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Compensation reflects the level of job responsibility, individual performance, and Company performance. As employee&#8217;s progress to higher levels in the organization, an increasing proportion of their pay should be linked to Company performance and stockholder returns because those employees are more able to affect Qualstar&#8217;s operating results.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>Compensation reflects the value of the job in the marketplace. To attract and retain a highly skilled work force, we must remain competitive with the pay of other employers who compete with us for talent.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-left:36pt'><KBD style='position:absolute;font:10pt Symbol;margin-left:-18pt'><FONT style=font-family:Symbol>&#183;</FONT></KBD>While compensation programs and individual pay levels will always reflect differences in job responsibilities, geographies and marketplace considerations, the overall structure of the compensation and benefit programs should be broadly similar and equitable across the organization.&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>

The assumptions used in calculating the aggregate grant date fair value of the awards reported in the column are set forth in our financial statements included in this Registration Statement. The amounts reported in this column reflect the accounting cost for these awards and do not correspond to the actual economic value that may be received by the named executive officers for the awards.&nbsp;</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>Components of Executive Compensation</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>For the twelve months ended December 31, 2025, the principal components of compensation for named executive officers were: (1) base salary, (2) performance-based incentive compensation, (3) long-term equity incentive compensation, (4) personal benefits, and (5) other compensation. In determining the amount and relative allocation among each component of compensation for each named executive officer, the Board (or in the case of Mr. Bronson, Mr. Wolenski, as the sole non-executive director on the Board) considered, among other factors, the Company&#8217;s and each executive officer&#8217;s experience level and historical performance, compensation paid by companies comparable in size to Qualstar, data obtained from management&#8217;s recruitment activities, historical rates of executive compensation, Company revenues and profitability, and alignment with the Company&#8217;s overall compensation philosophy. </P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>36</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt'><B><I>Base Salary</I></B>. Base salaries were set at levels that the Board deemed to be sufficient to attract and retain highly talented executive officers capable of fulfilling the Company&#8217;s key objectives. Base salaries were also set with the goal of rewarding executive officers on a day-to-day basis for their time and services while encouraging them to strive for performance-based and long-term incentives.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt'><B><I>Performance-Based Incentive Compensation</I></B>. The Company utilizes an annual discretionary cash bonus program, which is intended to reward executive officers based on the Company&#8217;s overall performance and the individual named executive officer&#8217;s contributions to that performance. In determining an annual discretionary bonus for each named executive officer, we evaluate performance as measured against certain objective financial metrics as well as individual performance goals. We believe that the performance-based incentive compensation provides incentives that are necessary to retain executives and reward them for our short-term performance in the pursuit of our larger business objectives and is designed to provide for a portion of our cash compensation for named executive officers to be variable based upon Company and individual performance.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt'><B><I>Long-Term Equity Incentive Compensation</I></B>. The Company has a long-term equity incentive plan, which is intended to retain executive officers and reward executive officers based on the Company&#8217;s performance. Equity incentives, such as stock options and restricted stock awards, have been granted to executive officers as long-term incentives in order to align executives&#8217; performance with the interests of the Company&#8217;s stockholders and also to encourage retention. No equity incentives were granted to executive officers in the twelve months ended December 31, 2025.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:36pt'><B><I>Personal Benefits</I></B>. As employees, the Company&#8217;s executives are eligible to participate in health and welfare benefits, as offered to our general workforce, designed to attract and retain a skilled workforce in a competitive marketplace. These benefits help ensure that the Company has a healthy and focused workforce through reliable and competitive health and other personal benefits. These benefits were considered in relation to the total compensation package but did not materially impact decisions regarding other elements of executive officer compensation.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The Company also maintains a tax-qualified retirement plan (&#8220;401(k) Plan&#8221;) that provides eligible employees with an opportunity to save for retirement on a tax-advantaged basis. All employees are eligible to participate in the 401(k) Plan following three months of service of employment and may contribute up to 100% of their compensation on a pre-tax basis, not to exceed the annual IRS maximum. The Company makes matching contributions in an amount equal to 50% of compensation contributed by eligible participants, up to $5,000 per participant per year.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Employment Agreement with Steven N. Bronson</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Effective February 1, 2024, the Company entered into an employment agreement with Mr. Bronson (the &#8220;Employment Agreement&#8221;), replacing a prior agreement, pursuant to which Mr. Bronson continued to serve as the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer and President. As since amended, the Employment Agreement expires on January 31, 2027. The Employment Agreement expressly provides that Mr. Bronson is not required to devote his full business time and energies to the Company, but is required to use his best efforts, skills and abilities to perform his duties and obligations to the Company.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The Employment Agreement provides for Mr. Bronson to receive an annual base salary of $250,000, and he is eligible to earn an annual bonus of up to 50% of his base salary based on the Company&#8217;s achievement of financial objectives established by the Board and Mr. Bronson&#8217;s achievement of agreed personal business objectives, with any bonus determined in the sole discretion of the Board. Mr. Bronson is also eligible to participate in benefit plans generally available to officers of the Company and to accrue five weeks of paid time off per year, subject to a maximum accrual of 300 hours.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>In connection with the execution of the Employment Agreement, on February 13, 2024, the Company granted Mr. Bronson a non-qualified stock option to purchase 300,000 shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock at an exercise price of $1.48 per share. The option vested with respect to 150,000 shares on each of February 1, 2025 and February 1, 2026 and expires on February 13, 2034, subject to earlier termination in accordance with its terms.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>37</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Under the terms of the Employment Agreement, Mr. Bronson is entitled to terminate his employment upon at least 90 days&#8217; written notice, and the Company can terminate his employment for Cause or without Cause. If Mr. Bronson&#8217;s employment is terminated by the Company without &#8220;Cause&#8221; or by Mr. Bronson for &#8220;Good Reason&#8221; (as such terms are defined), he is entitled, subject to execution and non-revocation of a separation agreement containing a release of claims and compliance with his obligations to the Company, to receive (i) 12 months of base salary, (ii) a pro-rated portion of his bonus for the applicable year, (iii) Company-paid COBRA benefits for up to 12 months and (iv) accelerated vesting of all outstanding unvested equity awards. Upon termination due to death or disability, Mr. Bronson or his beneficiaries are entitled, subject to the applicable conditions, to accelerated vesting of outstanding unvested equity awards and a pro-rated portion of his annual bonus.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The Employment Agreement also provides that if, within 180 days following a &#8220;Change in Control&#8221; (as defined), Mr. Bronson&#8217;s employment is terminated by the Company without Cause or by Mr. Bronson for Good Reason, he is  entitled, subject to the applicable conditions, to the severance benefits described above. The agreement contains customary confidentiality and proprietary information provisions that survive termination of employment.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><A name=item7 /><B>ITEM 7. CERTAIN RELATIONSHIPS AND RELATED TRANSACTIONS, AND DIRECTOR INDEPENDENCE</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>Transactions with Related Persons</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>During the past two fiscal years and through the date of this Registration Statement, the Company has engaged in various transactions involving related persons, including transactions involving former management, control persons, affiliated entities, and current management.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Interlink Electronics, Inc.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><BR>Interlink is a related party. Steven N. Bronson, our President and Chief Executive Officer and Director, is also Chairman of the Board, President and Chief Executive Officer of Interlink, and Ryan J. Hoffman, our Acting Chief Financial Officer, is also the Chief Financial Officer of Interlink. Mr. Bronson, together with BKF Capital (which he controls), has a controlling interest in both Qualstar and Interlink. We have a mutual facilities sharing agreement with Interlink under which (i) we allow Interlink to use of a portion of our Camarillo, California office and warehouse facility, and Interlink allowed us to use (while Interlink occupied such facilities) a portion of its former office facilities in Irvine, California and Bellevue, Washington; and (ii) we have agreed to split substantially all rent and facilities-related costs for each location on an apportioned basis according to the approximate relative usage levels by each entity. In addition, we have a mutual consulting agreement with Interlink under which certain of our respective employees and/or independent contractors provide certain operational, sales, marketing, general and administrative services to the other entity. Qualstar and Interlink have also agreed to reimburse, or be reimbursed by, one another for certain expenses paid by one company on behalf of the other.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>BKF Capital Group, Inc.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><BR>BKF Capital is a related party. Steven N. Bronson, our President and Chief Executive Officer and Director, is also the Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board of BKF Capital, and Ryan J. Hoffman, our Acting Chief Financial Officer, is also the Chief Financial Officer of BKF Capital. BKF Capital, together with Mr. Bronson, has a controlling interest in Qualstar. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><BR><B><I>Ridgefield Acquisition Corp.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><BR>Ridgefield Acquisition Corp. (OTCMKTS: RDGA) (&#8220;<B><I>Ridgefield</I></B>&#8221;) is a related party. Steven N. Bronson, our President and Chief Executive Officer and Director, is also the Chief Executive Officer and Chairman of the Board of Ridgefield as well as Ridgefield&#8217;s largest shareholder. Ryan J. Hoffman, our Chief Financial Officer, is also the Chief Financial Officer of Ridgefield. In September 2022, the Company executed an unsecured Revolving Promissory Note with Ridgefield (the &#8220;<B><I>Ridgefield Note</I></B>&#8221;). Under the terms of the Ridgefield Note, the Company may (but is not required to) make loans to Ridgefield from time to time upon request by Ridgefield, up to a maximum principal amount of $250,000. The Ridgefield Note may be prepaid by Ridgefield at any time without penalty and is repayable on demand by the Company. The Ridgefield Note provides for interest to accrue on the outstanding principal balance at a rate of 10%  per annum compounded quarterly. Ridgefield borrowed $50,000 under the Ridgefield Note in 2022, $50,000 in 2023, $10,000 in 2024, and $75,887 in 2025. The balance of principal and accrued interest on the Ridgefield Note was $185,887 and $36,709, respectively, at December 31, 2025; and was $110,000 and $19,946, respectively, at December 31, 2024 (classified in Prepaid Expenses and Other Current Assets on our consolidated balance sheets).</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>39</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Cost-Sharing Arrangements</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We have entered into the following cost-sharing arrangements with Interlink and BKF Capital:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><KBD style=margin-left:36pt></KBD><B><I>Facilities Agreements</I></B>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;text-indent:54pt'><I>Camarillo, California Facility:</I>&#160;We have a facilities agreement with Interlink to allow them to use a portion of the office and warehouse facility leased by us in Camarillo, California, and we have agreed to split substantially all rent and lease-related costs on an apportioned basis according to the approximate relative usage levels by each entity. For the years ended December&#160;31, 2025 and 2024, we billed Interlink $85,000 and $79,000, respectively, for its use of our Camarillo facility.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt;text-indent:54pt'><I>Irvine, California Facility:</I>&#160;We entered into facilities agreements with both Interlink and BKF Capital to allow each of them the use of a portion of the office previously leased by us in Irvine, California, under which we agreed to split substantially all rent and lease-related costs on an apportioned basis according to the approximate relative usage levels by each entity. For the years ended December&#160;31, 2025 and 2024, Interlink billed us $21,000 and $19,000, respectively, for our use of Interlink&#8217;s former Irvine office facility.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;text-indent:54pt'><I>Bellevue, Washington Facility:&#160;</I>We entered into a facilities agreement with Interlink to allow us to use a portion of the office previously leased by Interlink in Bellevue, Washington, under which we agreed to split substantially all rent and lease-related costs on an apportioned basis according to the approximate relative usage levels by each entity. For the years ended December&#160;31, 2025 and 2024, Interlink billed us $17,000 and $17,000, respectively, for our use of Interlink&#8217;s former Bellevue office facility.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>&#160;</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><KBD style=margin-left:36pt></KBD><B><I>Consulting Agreements</I></B>. We have entered into various consulting agreements with Interlink pursuant to which certain of the parties&#8217; respective employees and independent contractors provide operational, sales, marketing, general and administrative services to the other entity. Interlink provided such consulting services to us in the amounts of $288,000 and $335,000 for the years ended December&#160;31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. Qualstar provided such consulting services to Interlink in the amounts of $59,000 and $58,000 for the years ended December&#160;31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. &nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><KBD style=margin-left:36pt></KBD><B><I>Expense Reimbursements</I></B>. Interlink, Qualstar and BKF Capital occasionally pay expenses on behalf of one another, for which each party reimburses the other party correspondingly. We incurred reimbursable expenses on behalf of Interlink in the amounts of $43,000 and $21,000 for the years ended December&#160;31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. Interlink incurred reimbursable expenses on behalf of us in the amounts of $102,000 and $79,000 for the years ended December&#160;31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. Expenses incurred by us and BKF Capital on behalf of the other party were immaterial for years ended December&#160;31, 2025 and 2024.<B>&#160;</B>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'><B><I>Director Independence</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin-top:0pt;margin-bottom:6pt'>The Company current has two members of its Board of Directors. The Board of Directors has determined that David Wolenski qualifies as an &#8220;independent director&#8221; under generally recognized corporate governance standards applicable to public companies. Steven N. Bronson is the Company&#8217;s Chief Executive Officer and President, and as such does not qualify as an independent director. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Other than the transactions described above, there have been no transactions since the beginning of the Company&#8217;s last fiscal year, or any currently proposed transactions, in which the Company was or is to be a participant and in which any director, executive officer, or beneficial owner of more than five percent (5%) of the Company&#8217;s common stock had or will have a direct or indirect material interest that would be required to be disclosed pursuant to Item 404(a) of Regulation S-K.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Policies and Procedures for Related-Party Transactions </I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The Company does not currently have formal written policies or procedures governing the review, approval, or ratification of related-party transactions. In practice, the Company&#8217;s Board of Directors reviews and approves all related-party transactions and matters involving potential conflicts of interest, with consideration given to the fairness of the transaction, the best interests of the Company, and applicable legal and regulatory requirements.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><A name=item12 /><B>ITEM 12. INDEMNIFICATION OF DIRECTORS AND OFFICERS.</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Section 78.138 of the Nevada Revised Statutes provides that directors and officers, in deciding upon matters of business, are presumed to act in good faith, on an informed basis and with a view to the interests of the corporation. A director or officer is not individually liable to the corporation or its stockholders or creditors for damages as a result of any act or failure to act in his or her capacity as a director or officer unless that presumption is rebutted and it is proven that (1) the director&#8217;s or officer&#8217;s act or failure to act constituted a breach of his or her fiduciary duties as a director or officer and (2) such breach involved intentional misconduct, fraud or a knowing violation of law.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>This provision limits the potential liability of directors and officers for monetary damages resulting from suits alleging a breach of fiduciary duty. As a consequence of this provision, stockholders of the Company generally will be unable to recover monetary damages against directors or officers for actions or omissions that may constitute negligence or gross negligence in the performance of their duties unless the requirements described above are satisfied. The provision, however, does not alter the applicable standards governing a director&#8217;s or officer&#8217;s fiduciary duties and does not eliminate or limit the right of the Company or any stockholder to seek injunctive or other non-monetary relief in the event of a breach of fiduciary duty.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The Company&#8217;s Articles of Incorporation eliminate, to the fullest extent permitted by the NRS, the personal liability of the Company&#8217;s directors and officers to the Company or its stockholders for monetary damages for breach of fiduciary duty as a director or officer, except for acts or omissions that involve intentional misconduct, fraud, or a knowing violation of law. The Articles provide for mandatory indemnification of directors and officers against all liabilities and expenses (including attorneys&#8217; fees, judgments, fines, and amounts paid in settlement) actually and reasonably incurred in connection with a threatened, pending, or completed proceeding, if the person acted in good faith and in a manner the person reasonably believed to be in or not opposed to the best interests of the Company and, with respect to any criminal proceeding, had no reasonable cause to believe the person&#8217;s conduct was unlawful. The Articles also provide for advancement of expenses upon receipt of an undertaking to repay the amounts if it is ultimately determined that the person is not entitled to indemnification. Section 78.7502 of the Nevada Revised Statutes further provides for discretionary indemnification of directors, officers, employees and agents under specified circumstances, including where the person is not liable pursuant to NRS 78.138 or acted in good faith and in a manner the person reasonably believed to be in or not opposed to the best interests of the corporation and, with respect to any criminal action or proceeding, had no reasonable cause to believe the person&#8217;s conduct was unlawful.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Our Bylaws provide mandatory indemnification of directors and officers against all expenses (including attorneys&#8217; fees), judgments, fines, and amounts paid in settlement actually and reasonably incurred in connection with proceedings. Indemnification is mandatory unless a determination is made under applicable law that the indemnitee is not entitled to indemnification, and any such denial requires a specific finding, based on clear and convincing evidence, that the conduct constituted intentional misconduct, fraud, or a knowing violation of law. Under the Bylaws, the Company must advance expenses upon receipt of a written undertaking to repay the amounts if indemnification is ultimately unavailable, and advancement continues through all levels of appeal. Additionally, our Bylaws exculpate directors and officers from personal liability to the fullest extent permitted by law, subject to the exceptions described above. These indemnification and advancement rights are contractual, vest upon commencement of service, and continue thereafter, including after service ends.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>Insofar as indemnification for liabilities arising under the Securities Act may be permitted to directors, officers or persons controlling the registrant pursuant to the foregoing provisions, we have been informed that in the opinion of the SEC such indemnification is against the public policy as expressed in the Securities Act and is therefore unenforceable.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We have obtained liability insurance for the benefit of our directors and officers which provides coverage for losses of directors and officers for liabilities arising out of claims against such persons acting as directors or officers of the registrant (or any subsidiary thereof) due to any breach of duty, neglect, error, misstatement, misleading statement, omission or act done by such directors and officers, except as prohibited by law.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Opinion on the Financial Statements</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Qualstar Corporation (the Company) as of December&#160;31, 2025 and 2024, and the related consolidated statements of operations, shareholders&#8217; equity, and cash flows for the years then ended, and the related notes (collectively referred to as the &#8220;financial statements&#8221;). In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the Company as of December&#160;31, 2025 and 2024, and the results of its operations and its cash flows for the years then ended in conformity with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Basis for Opinion</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>These financial statements are the responsibility of the entity&#8217;s management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our audits. We are a public accounting firm registered with the Public Company Accounting Oversight Board (United States) (&quot;PCAOB&quot;) and are required to be independent with respect to the Company in accordance with the U.S. federal securities laws and the applicable rules and regulations of the Securities and Exchange Commission and the PCAOB. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>We conducted our audits in accordance with the standards of the PCAOB. Those standards require that we plan and perform the audits to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material misstatement, whether due to error or fraud. The Company is not required to have, nor were we engaged to perform, an audit of its internal control over financial reporting. As part of our audits we are required to obtain an understanding of internal control over financial reporting but not for the purpose of expressing an opinion on the effectiveness of the entity&#8217;s internal control over financial reporting. Accordingly, we express no such opinion.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Our audits included performing procedures to assess the risks of material misstatement of the financial statements, whether due to error or fraud, and performing procedures that respond to those risks. Such procedures included examining, on a test basis, evidence regarding the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. Our audits also included evaluating the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by management, as well as evaluating the overall presentation of the financial statements. We believe that our audits provide a reasonable basis for our opinion.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Critical Audit Matters</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Critical audit matters are matters arising from the current period audit of the financial statements that were communicated or required to be communicated to the audit committee and that: (1) relate to accounts or disclosures that are material to the financial statements and (2) involved our especially challenging, subjective, or complex judgments. We determined that there are no critical audit matters.</P>

<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>QUALSTAR CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</B></P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><A name=note /><B>Note&#160;1&#160;&#8211;&#160;Significant Accounting Policies</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Business</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Qualstar Corporation and its Subsidiaries (&#8220;Qualstar&#8221;, the &#8220;Company&#8221;, &#8220;we&#8221;, &#8220;us&#8221; or &#8220;our&#8221;) manufacture and market data storage system products and compact, high-efficiency power supply solutions. Our data storage systems are marketed under the Qualstar brand and include highly scalable automated magnetic tape libraries used to store, retrieve and manage electronic data primarily in the network computing environment. Our data storage devices include models ranging from entry level to enterprise and are a cost-effective solution for organizations requiring backup, recovery and archival storage of critical electronic information. The distribution channels for our data storage devices include resellers, system integrators, and original equipment manufacturers (&#8220;OEMs&#8221;). In addition, the Company is a leading provider of standard, semi-custom and custom power supply solutions marketed under the N2Power brand. Our power supply solution products provide OEMs and product designers increased functionality while reducing thermal loads and cooling requirements and lowering operating costs. Our power supply solution products are currently sold to OEMs in a wide range of markets, including telecom/networking equipment, audio/visual, industrial, gaming and medical.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Qualstar Corporation was incorporated in California in 1984 and was re-incorporated in Nevada in 2026 and currently has three wholly owned subsidiaries. The N2Power, Inc. subsidiary (&#8220;N2Power&#8221;) operates the Company&#8217;s power supplies business. The Q-Smart Data Limited (China) subsidiary pursues new data storage business opportunities in Asia. The Qualstar Limited (U.K.) subsidiary supports expansion of the Company&#8217;s data storage business in the United Kingdom, Europe and Africa.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>We sell our products globally through authorized resellers and distributors and directly to OEMs. Our data storage products are manufactured by our OEM suppliers in other parts of the world and configured to order by us at our facility in Camarillo, California, or at our facility in Shenzhen, China, or by our fulfilment and logistics partner in Warsaw, Poland. N2Power utilizes contract manufacturers in Asia to produce our power supply solutions products.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>April 2026 Stock Split</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>In connection with its reincorporation in Nevada, the Company effected a 3-for-1 forward stock split effective April 8, 2026. The stock split increased the number of issued and outstanding shares of common stock from 1,380,853 to 4,142,559 at that time. Except as otherwise noted, all references to common stock, common stock issuable upon exercise of stock options, and corresponding per share information throughout this Annual Report have been retroactively adjusted to reflect the stock split.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Principles of Consolidation</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>The consolidated financial statements include our accounts and the accounts of each of our wholly owned subsidiaries: N2Power, Inc., Q-Smart Data Limited (China), and Qualstar Limited (U.K.). All significant intercompany accounts and transactions have been eliminated in consolidation.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Estimates and Assumptions </I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Preparing financial statements in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States of America (&#8220;GAAP&#8221;) requires management to make estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets, liabilities, revenue, and expenses. Examples include estimates of loss contingencies, product life cycles and inventory obsolescence, credit loss bad debts, sales returns, warranty costs, share-based compensation forfeiture rates, the tax consequences of events that have been recognized in our consolidated financial statements or tax returns, and determinations as to when investment impairments are other-than-temporary. Actual results and outcomes may differ from management&#8217;s estimates and assumptions.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>F-6</P>
<HR style='page-break-after:always;border:0;height:3pt;background-color:#909090;margin:8pt 0'><P style=line-height:0;margin:0></P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>QUALSTAR CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</B></P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Revenue Recognition</I></B>&#160;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>The Company recognizes revenue when its customer obtains control of promised goods or services, in an amount that reflects the consideration which we expect to receive in exchange for those goods or services. To determine revenue recognition for arrangements that the Company determines are within the scope of ASC&#160;606, we perform the following five steps: (i)&#160;identify the contract(s) with a customer; (ii)&#160;identify the performance obligations in the contract; (iii)&#160;determine the transaction price; (iv)&#160;allocate the transaction price to the performance obligations in the contract; and (v)&#160;recognize revenue when (or as) we satisfy a performance obligation. The five-step model is applied to contracts when it is probable that we will collect the consideration we are entitled to in exchange for the goods or services transferred to the customer. At contract inception, once the contract is determined to be within the scope of ASC&#160;606, we assess the goods or services promised within each contract and determine those that are performance obligations and assess whether each promised good or service is distinct. We then recognize revenue in the amount of the transaction price that is allocated to the respective performance obligation when (or as) the performance obligation is satisfied.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>We derive revenues from two primary sources: products and services. Product revenue includes the shipment of product according to the agreement with our customers for data storage products and power supplies. Services include customer support (technical support), installations, consulting, and design services. A contract may include both product and services. Rarely, contracts with customers contain multiple performance obligations. For these contracts, the Company accounts for individual performance obligations separately if they are distinct. The transaction price is allocated to the separate performance obligations on a relative standalone selling price basis. Standalone selling prices are typically estimated based on observable transactions when these services are sold on a standalone basis. Title and risk of loss generally pass to our customers upon shipment and therefore revenue is recognized at the time goods are shipped to the customers. In limited circumstances where either title or risk of loss pass upon destination, we defer revenue recognition until such events occur.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>A variety of technical services can be contracted by our customers for a designated period of time. The service contracts allow customers to call Qualstar for technical support, to have defective parts replaced and to have onsite service provided by Qualstar&#8217;s third-party contract service provider. We record revenue for contract services at the amount of the service contract, but such amount is deferred at the beginning of the service term and amortized ratably over the life of the contract.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Deferred service revenue is shown separately in the consolidated balance sheets as current and long term. At December&#160;31, 2025, we had deferred service revenue of approximately $998,000. At December&#160;31, 2024, we had deferred service revenue of approximately $1,073,000.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Cash and Cash Equivalents</I></B></P>

<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>QUALSTAR CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</B></P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B>NOTES TO CONSOLIDATED FINANCIAL STATEMENTS</B></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Allowance for Expected Credit Losses</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>The Company records accounts receivable at invoiced amounts, net of an allowance for expected credit losses. Accounts receivable are generally unsecured and arise from the sale of goods to customers in the ordinary course of business. The Company does not charge interest on past due accounts. Accounts are written off against the allowance when management determines they are uncollectible.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-right:7.5pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>The allowance for expected credit losses represents management&#8217;s estimate of lifetime expected credit losses on accounts receivable. In estimating the allowance, the Company considers historical credit loss experience, current economic conditions, and forecasts of estimated future conditions. </P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-right:7.5pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Accounts receivable consisted of the following:</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Inventories</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Inventories are stated at the lower of cost (first in, first out basis) or net realizable value. Cost includes materials, labor, and manufacturing overhead related to the purchase and production of inventories. We regularly review inventory quantities on hand, future purchase commitments with our suppliers, and the estimated utility of our inventory. If our review indicates a reduction in utility below carrying value, we reduce our inventory to a new cost basis.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Property and Equipment, net</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Property and equipment are recorded at cost less accumulated depreciation and amortization. Depreciation expense is computed using the straight-line method. Leasehold improvements are amortized over the shorter of the estimated useful life of the asset or the term of the lease. Estimated useful lives are as follows:</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<TABLE style=border-collapse:collapse;width:100%><TR><TD valign=top style=width:11.54%><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
</TD><TD valign=top style=width:29.8%><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Machinery and equipment</P>
</TD><TD valign=top style=width:58.66%><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>5-7 years</P>
</TD></TR>
<TR><TD valign=top style=width:11.54%><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
</TD><TD valign=top style=width:29.8%><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Furniture and fixtures</P>
</TD><TD valign=top style=width:58.66%><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>5-7 years</P>

</TD></TR>
</TABLE>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Expenditures for normal maintenance and repairs are charged to expense as incurred, and improvements are capitalized. Upon the sale or retirement of property or equipment, the asset cost and related accumulated depreciation are removed from the respective accounts and any gain or loss is included in the results of operations.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Long-Lived Assets</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Qualstar evaluates long-lived assets for potential impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying amount of any asset may not be recoverable. An impairment loss would be recognized when the estimated undiscounted future cash flows expected to result from the use of the asset and its eventual disposition is less than the carrying amount. If impairment is indicated, the amount of the loss to be recorded is based upon an estimate of the difference between the carrying amount and the fair value of the asset. Fair value is based upon discounted cash flows expected to result from the use of the asset and its eventual disposition and other valuation methods. No impairment losses of long-lived assets were recognized during the periods presented.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Warranty Obligations</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>A provision for costs related to warranty expense is recorded when revenue is recognized, which is estimated based on historical warranty costs incurred.</P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>F-8</P>
