<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>Note&#160;9&#160;&#8211;&#160;Related Party Transactions</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B><I>Interlink Electronics, Inc.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Interlink Electronics, Inc. (Nasdaq: LINK) is a related party. Steven N. Bronson, our President, CEO, and Director, is also Chairman of the Board, President and CEO of Interlink. Ryan J. Hoffman, our CFO, is also the CFO of Interlink. Mr. Bronson, together with BKF Capital Group, Inc. (&#8220;BKF Capital&#8221;) which he controls, has a controlling interest in both Qualstar and Interlink. We have a mutual facilities sharing agreement with Interlink under which (i) we allow Interlink to use of a portion of our Camarillo, California office and warehouse facility, and Interlink allowed us to use (while Interlink occupied such facilities) a portion of its former office facilities in Irvine, California and Bellevue, Washington; and (ii) we have agreed to split substantially all rent and facilities-related costs for each location on an apportioned basis according to the approximate relative usage levels by each entity. In addition, we have a mutual consulting agreement with Interlink under which certain of our respective employees and/or independent contractors provide certain operational, sales, marketing, general and administrative services to the other entity. Qualstar and Interlink have also agreed to reimburse, or be reimbursed by, one another for certain expenses paid by one company on behalf of the other. Transactions with Interlink are as follows:</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-right:7.5pt;color:#000000'><B><I>Ridgefield Acquisition Corp.</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-right:7.5pt;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Ridgefield Acquisition Corp. (OTCMKTS: RDGA) (&#8220;Ridgefield&#8221;) is a related party. Steven N. Bronson, our President, CEO and Director, is also the CEO and Chairman of the Board of Ridgefield as well as Ridgefield&#8217;s largest shareholder. Ryan J. Hoffman, our CFO, is also the CFO of Ridgefield. In 2022, the Company executed an unsecured Revolving Promissory Note with Ridgefield (the &#8220;Ridgefield Note&#8221;). Under the terms of the Ridgefield Note, the Company may (but is not required to) make loans to Ridgefield from time to time upon request by Ridgefield, up to a maximum principal amount of $250,000 (as amended). The Ridgefield Note may be prepaid by Ridgefield at any time without penalty and is repayable on demand by the Company. The Ridgefield Note provides for interest to accrue on the outstanding principal balance at a rate of ten percent per annum compounded quarterly. Ridgefield borrowed $50,000 under the Ridgefield Note in 2022, $50,000 in 2023, $10,000 in 2024, $75,887 in 2025, and $45,447 in 2026. The balance of principal and accrued interest on the Ridgefield Note was $231,334 and $49,832, respectively, at June&#160;30, 2026; and was $185,887 and $36,709, respectively, at December&#160;31, 2025 (classified in Prepaid Expenses and Other Current Assets on our consolidated balance sheets).</P>

<DIV style=margin-left:72pt;width:468pt><P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>QUALSTAR CORPORATION AND SUBSIDIARIES</B></P>
<P style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&#160;</P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B>MANAGEMENT&#8217;S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION</B></P>
<P align=center style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><B>AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</B></P>
<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><A name=mda1 /><B><I>Overview</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Qualstar Corporation and its subsidiaries (&#8220;Qualstar&#8221;, the &#8220;Company&#8221;, &#8220;we&#8221;, &#8220;us&#8221; or &#8220;our&#8221;) manufacture and market data storage system products and compact, high-efficiency power supply solutions. Our data storage systems are marketed under the Qualstar brand and include highly scalable automated magnetic tape libraries used to store, retrieve and manage electronic data primarily in the network computing environment. Our data storage devices include models ranging from entry level to enterprise and are a cost-effective solution for organizations requiring backup, recovery and archival storage of critical electronic information. The distribution channels for our data storage devices include resellers, system integrators, and original equipment manufacturers (&#8220;OEMs&#8221;). In addition, the Company is a leading provider of standard, semi-custom and custom power supply solutions marketed under the N2Power brand. Our power supply solution products provide OEMs and product designers increased functionality while reducing thermal loads and cooling requirements and lowering operating costs. Our power supply solution products are currently sold to OEMs in a wide range of markets, including telecom/networking equipment, audio/visual, industrial, gaming and medical.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Qualstar Corporation was incorporated in California in 1984 and re-incorporated in Nevada in April 2026. &nbsp;The Company has three wholly owned subsidiaries: N2Power, Inc. (&#8220;N2Power&#8221;), which operates the Company&#8217;s power supplies business; Q-Smart Data Limited (China), which pursues new data storage business opportunities in Asia; and Qualstar Limited (U.K.), which supports expansion of the Company&#8217;s data storage business in the United Kingdom, Europe and Africa.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-right:7.2pt;color:#000000'>We sell our products globally through authorized resellers and distributors and directly to OEMs. Our data storage products are manufactured by our OEM suppliers in other parts of the world and configured to order by us at our facility in Camarillo, California, or at our facility in Shenzhen, China, or by our fulfilment and logistics partner in Warsaw, Poland. N2Power utilizes contract manufacturers in Asia to produce our power supply solutions products.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-right:7.2pt'>&nbsp;</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>The fluctuations in revenues for the three and six months ended June&#160;30, 2026 compared to the prior year are attributable to the segment-specific factors described below.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><A name=_Hlk496797722 />&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B>Segment Revenue</B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'><A name=_Hlk159597046 /><B><I>Data Storage</I></B> &#8211;&nbsp;For the three months ended June&#160;30, 2026 compared to the same quarter last year, data storage revenues were up 58%, which was attributable to an 80% increase in product revenue from higher shipments of our tape-based data storage products and solutions, offset in part by a 19% decrease in revenues from technical service and support contracts. For the six months ended June&#160;30, 2026 compared to the same period last year, data storage revenues were up 31%, which was attributable to a 46% increase in product revenue from higher shipments of our tape-based data storage products and solutions, offset in part by a 24% decrease in revenues from technical service and support contracts.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><A name=_Hlk157954912 /><B><I>Power Supplies</I></B> &#8211;&nbsp;The 14% and 50% decreases in power supplies revenues in the three-month and six-month periods ended June&#160;30, 2026, respectively, compared to the prior-year periods were due to decreased customer demand and order fulfilment of our power supplies products<A name=_Hlk181099083 />.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><A name=_Hlk213075953 />The decreases in gross profit and gross margin percentage for the three and six months ended June&#160;30, 2026 compared to the same periods last year were due to a net realizable value charge of approximately $970,000 recorded in June 2026 on our slow-moving power supplies inventory due to the decreased demand from our customers in this segment. Excluding this charge, gross margin percentages were 36.4% and 32.2% for the three and six months ended June&#160;30, 2026, respectively.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><A name=_Hlk158384126 /><B><I>Engineering</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><A name=_Hlk512414333 />Engineering expenses for the three- and six-month periods ended June 30, 2026 were generally consistent with the corresponding prior-year periods, except that the prior-year periods included $31,000 of Employee Retention Credits (ERCs), which reduced engineering expenses in those prior year periods.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Sales and Marketing </I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Sales and marketing expenses increased for the three- and six-month periods ended June 30, 2026 compared with the corresponding prior-year periods due to higher marketing and promotional activities and trade show costs, as well as the absence of $63,000 and $119,000 of ERCs recorded in the prior-year three- and six-month periods, respectively, which reduced sales and marketing expenses in those prior year periods.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-right:15pt'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>General and Administrative </I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>General and administrative expenses for the three- and six-month periods ended June 30, 2026 were generally consistent with the corresponding prior-year periods, except that the six-month period ended June&#160;30, 2025 included ERCs of $39,000, which reduced general and administrative expenses in that prior year period.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;margin-right:37.5pt'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Other Income (Expense)</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Other income (expense) for the three months ended June&#160;30, 2026 included $10,000 of interest income and $301,000 of losses on marketable securities. Other income (expense) for the three months ended June&#160;30, 2025 included $35,000 of interest income, $8,000 of gains on foreign currency exchange, and $156,000 of gains on marketable securities. Other income (expense) for the six months ended June&#160;30, 2026 included $23,000 of interest income, $1,000 of losses on foreign currency exchange, and $139,000 of losses on marketable securities. Other income (expense) for the six months ended June&#160;30, 2025 included $76,000 of interest income, $27,000 of gains on foreign currency exchange, and $145,000 of gains on marketable securities.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Cash and cash equivalents decreased $739,000 to $1,129,000 at June&#160;30, 2026, from $1,868,000 at December&#160;31, 2025.</P>

<HR style='border:0;height:0;width:0;margin:14pt 0 0 0'><P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Operating Activities</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Net cash used in operating activities was $675,000 for the six months ended June&#160;30, 2026, compared with cash provided by operating activities of $208,000 for the first half of 2025. Cash used in operating activities in 2026 was the result of net loss of $1,164,000, non-cash expenses of $18,000, non-cash losses on marketable securities of $139,000, and cash provided by changes in operating assets and liabilities of $332,000. Cash provided by operations in 2025 was the result of net income of $387,000, non-cash expenses of $100,000, gains on marketable securities of $204,000, and cash used in changes in operating assets and liabilities of $75,000.</P>

<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Investing Activities</I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>Cash used in investing activities for the six months ended June&#160;30, 2026 and 2025 consisted of $64,000 and $202,000, respectively, of net purchases of marketable securities.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'><B><I>Financing Activities </I></B></P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>No cash was provided by or used in financing activities for the six months ended June&#160;30, 2026. Cash used in financing activities for the six months ended June&#160;30, 2025 consisted of $218,000 used to repurchase shares of the Company&#8217;s common stock under the Company&#8217;s Stock Repurchase Program.</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>&nbsp;</P>
<P align=justify style='font:10pt Times New Roman;margin:0;color:#000000'>We believe that our existing cash and cash equivalents and cash flows from our operating activities will be sufficient to fund our working capital and capital expenditure needs for at least twelve months from the date of this report. We may utilize cash to invest in or acquire businesses, products or technologies that we believe are additive to the strategic expansion of the Company. We periodically evaluate other companies and technologies for possible investment or acquisition. In addition, we have made, and may in the future make, investments in companies with whom we have identified potential synergies. However, we have no present commitments or agreements with respect to any material investment in or acquisition of other businesses or technologies. In the event that we require additional capital to meet our business needs, there can be no assurance that additional funding will be available to us when needed or, if available, that it can be obtained on commercially reasonable terms.</P>
